transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well... my regular doctor suggested I come in. He seems concerned that my meal planning has gotten... too tight, I guess. 

I don't really see it that way, honestly. To me, it just feels like keeping breakfast to a yogurt, and... maybe skipping lunch if I’m busy. Then I just make a very measured dinner. It just keeps the day orderly. But he wanted me to see someone, so... here I am.
Do you feel anxious or upset when you can't stick to your meal plan?

Well... yes, I suppose. If things deviate and I have a normal dinner, or eat at a restaurant... and the scale is up even a pound the next morning... I get this sharp panic. It just feels like I've lost control of things. And then I feel like I need to correct it the next day. So I prefer to just stick to the plan.
Is your meal plan mainly to control your weight?

I suppose. I mean... I know I’m an older woman. I’m not trying to look young or anything like that. But... I do still judge how well I’m handling myself by... well, by whether my waist and hips look contained in my clothes. It just tells me I'm keeping things in order.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?

I suppose so. Like I mentioned a moment ago... if I eat a normal dinner out somewhere and the scale is up even a single pound the next day... I get that sharp panic. It just tells me I've lost control and I have to correct it. So... yes. I prefer to avoid that.
Do you worry that gaining weight would make you unhealthy?
I don't... no, not really. I don't really think about it in terms of my health. It's not... I haven't really focused on that part of it. It's just what I said before.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight recently?

It's... drifted down some. More than my regular doctor likes, I suppose. But... well, when I look at the chart, I just find myself thinking that a little lower would be... a cleaner number. Just more manageable.
Do you think you are currently underweight?

I don't... really see it that way. My physician tells me it's medically unsafe, but... I think she's overstating it. I'm still working. I run my own errands, I manage my life just fine. I'm functioning. So... no, I don't really think it's an issue.
Do you feel like your eating habits are the only thing in your life that you can control?
I... I wouldn't say that. I manage a lot of things. My work, my house... I have a handle on my life. It's just... this is one part of it. I don't really think about it like that.
Do you feel like not following your meal plan would lead to a loss of control in other areas of your life?
I... don't really see a connection there. I just prefer to stick to my routine. I don't think altering it would... ruin the rest of my life or anything. It's just how I prefer to do things.
Do you feel anxious about losing control in any areas of your life beyond just your eating habits?

I... no. Not really. I don't think I get anxious about things like that. I just... I like things to be orderly. In my line of work, you have to keep things organized, so... that's just how I operate. I don't really sit around worrying about losing control.
Do you have any fears about things spiraling out of control in your life outside of your eating habits?
No. I... I think I just said that, really. I don't have fears about things spiraling. Everything is fine. I just... I don't spend my time worrying about everything falling apart.
Are there any situations in your life, outside of eating, where you feel like things might get out of control?
I... I feel like you're asking me the exact same question again. I really don't know how else to answer it. No. There aren't. I manage my life just fine.
Do you think your weight has any impact on how attractive you feel?

I suppose... well, yes. I mean, I know I'm an older woman. I'm 63, I'm not trying to look young or anything like that. But... I still judge how well I'm handling myself by how my clothes fit. If my waist and hips look... contained. If they don't, I just... I don't feel good about myself.
Do you think gaining weight would make you less attractive?

I... yes. I suppose so. If the scale goes up even a pound... say, after a normal dinner or going out to a restaurant... I feel this sharp panic. It just feels like I've lost control, and I... I need to correct it the next day.
Is your fear of gaining weight mostly about feeling fat?

I... I think I just explained that. It's not really about using the word 'fat.' It's just... like I just mentioned, if the scale goes up even a single pound after a meal out, it brings on that panic. That feeling that I'm losing my grip and have to fix it the next day. I don't really know how else to describe it to you.
Is your fear of gaining weight more about feeling like you're losing control or about feeling less attractive?

I... well, like I just said, it's mostly the control. If the scale is up even a pound after a dinner out, I get that sharp panic. It's just... feeling like I've lost control of things and I have to correct it. That's really all I can say about it.
Do you think your weight is higher than it actually is?
I... no, I don't think so. I just go by the number on the scale. I don't really imagine it being higher than what it actually says.
Do you think your fear of gaining weight is mostly about how your body looks?

I... I feel like I just answered that. It's not really about the mirror, or how my body looks. It's just... the number on the scale, and keeping that where it should be. I don't really have anything else to add to it.
Do you think your body is a normal shape and size when you look in the mirror?

I mean... I know I'm an older woman. I'm not trying to look young or anything like that. But... I guess I just judge how well I'm handling myself by... by whether my waist and hips look contained in my clothes. That's really all I look for.
Do you think your body shape or size is abnormal when you look in the mirror?

No, I... I wouldn't say abnormal. I don't really stare at myself looking for things like that. Like I said, I just check that my clothes fit the way they're supposed to. I don't really dwell on it beyond that.
